body:
## Scope

This PR is **not** a solution for issue #49. It fixes one defect found on the way: the public gateway health document and the DevNet RPC helper can report wrong millisecond latencies, and request deadlines use the wrong unit. The #49 work that remains (owner-authorized `gdc ops site` / `gdc ops edge`, public inference acceptance, the DevShard v5 rollout, and the Gonka v0.2.16 transition) needs owner-held credentials and live infrastructure. This PR does not attempt any of it.

Part of #49.

## Defect and root cause

`https://gonka-dev.net/status/gateway-health` currently reports values like `"latency_ms": 19651863` and `23603745` for a probe that runs every few seconds.

The affected scripts took millisecond timestamps with `date +%s%3N`. Ubuntu 26.04, a supported Host OS, ships uutils coreutils 0.8.0 as `date`, and that `date` ignores the `%3N` width and prints unpadded nanoseconds:

| `date` implementation | `date +%s%3N` |
|---|---|
| GNU coreutils 9.1 / 9.4 | `1790273287205` (correct) |
| uutils 0.3.0 – 0.6.0 | 13 digits (correct) |
| uutils 0.7.0 | `1790273355137920493` |
| uutils 0.8.0 (stock `ubuntu:26.04` image) | `1790274278470608404` |
| uutils 0.9.0 – 0.12.0 | 13 digits (correct) |

These values were checked on 2026-09-24 with the upstream uutils release binaries and the `ubuntu:26.04` container. Because the output is unpadded, the difference between two readings is in nanoseconds, or garbage when the digit counts differ. Fed the uutils-0.7 behaviour, the unmodified `main` probe published `latency_ms: -1611246130079893093`.

## Change

- Every `date +%s%3N` in `04-ops/`, `scripts/`, and `devnet/node_scripts/find_best_rpc.sh` becomes `$(( ${EPOCHREALTIME//[!0-9]/} / 1000 ))`, the bash ≥ 5.0 builtin. Bash 5.3 on Ubuntu 26.04 and bash 5.1/5.2 on 22.04/24.04 provide it, and these scripts already need bash 4 features (`declare -A`, `mapfile`). No `date` subprocess, no shared helper file, and nothing new for `install-ops.sh` to deploy. This replaces the two copies of `epoch-millis.sh` from the earlier revision.
- The readiness waiter rejects a `completion_finished_ms` later than now + 1 s, so a probe host that still produces nanosecond receipts can't pass for fresh.
- The public health schema checks in `verify-public-homepage.sh` and `capture-gateway-observability.sh` bound `latency_ms` to `[0, 60000]` and require a 13-digit `completion_finished_ms` when it isn't zero.

## Tests

- `scripts/test-gateway-health-probe.sh` runs the real probe with a `date` on `PATH` that behaves like uutils 0.7/0.8, and asserts `latency_ms` is in `[0, 60000]` and `completion_finished_ms` has 13 digits. It fails against the `main` probe and passes on this branch.
- `scripts/test-public-traffic-readiness.sh` adds a nanosecond-scale future receipt, which must be rejected.
- `scripts/test-profiles.sh` fails if any `$(date …%3N)` comes back into `04-ops/` or `scripts/`.
- `devnet/node_scripts/test-find_best_rpc.sh` mocks uutils-style nanoseconds and RPC responses, then checks the reported latency is in milliseconds. It fails before this fix and passes afterward. The runbook workflow runs it on changes to either DevNet RPC file.
- Locally, `make shellcheck` (ShellCheck v0.11.0), the focused runbook tests above, and all 29 scripts after JOIN preflight pass. The new probe regression fails against unmodified `main` and passes on this branch.
- A full `make test` run from this `/tmp` checkout stops at `test-recovery-contract`: its persistent-output fixture rejects a world-writable parent. The same four assertions fail on unmodified `main`; that test passes from a `/home/box` worktree. With it skipped, the suite stops at the existing `test-join-preflight-diagnostics.sh` five-second observation deadline. The same test fails on `main` in this environment; a local run with a 15-second observation window passes all its assertions. No production deadline was changed.
- The exact-head runbook CI job is `action_required` with no jobs or logs. It still needs maintainer approval for this fork PR.

## Deployment status

Nothing is deployed by this PR. The live probe keeps reporting nanosecond latencies until an owner-authorized OPS reinstall puts the updated `gateway-health-probe.sh` on the gateway Host.



Fixes paranjko/external-test-lab#49

commits.messageBody:
Ubuntu 26.04 ships uutils coreutils 0.8.0, whose date ignores the %3N
width and prints unpadded nanoseconds (0.7.0 behaves the same; 0.9.0
fixed it). The gateway health probe on such a host published
multi-million latency_ms values and nanosecond request deadlines.

Replace the duplicated epoch-millis.sh helper with the bash builtin
EPOCHREALTIME, so neither the launcher nor the OPS bundle needs a
shared file or a date subprocess. The health probe test now runs the
real probe under a uutils-0.7-style date and fails on the old code.
commits.messageHeadline: fix(ops): read millisecond clocks from EPOCHREALTIME
fix(devnet): measure RPC latency in milliseconds with bash clock
